ink.description: Core primitive. Default text/heading color, the modal backdrop tint, and illustration fills — anywhere the old near-black needs replacing.

cyan-dark.description: Core primitive. The link color — resolves text-link.

cyan-700.description: Core primitive, retained from the original palette. Interactive emphasis and the primary button fill — resolves accent-primary and background-button-primary. (Merged with the former 'cyan-button' primitive — one less near-duplicate cyan.)

cyan-500.description: Core primitive, retained from the original palette. Bright accents and active surfaces — resolves accent-bright.

cyan-100.description: Core primitive, retained from the original palette. Pale interaction background — resolves background-link-hover.

border.description: Core primitive. Greyish-purple border/divider color — resolves border-default and border-button-secondary.

white.description: Core primitive. White and inverse text — resolves text-inverse and text-button-primary.

transparent.description: Core primitive. Fully transparent surface — resolves background-button-secondary.

background-01.description: Page-background pool (1 of 15, order preserved from the original homepage script). Selected once per page load and held stable for that page — never tied to a fixed section.

background-08.description: Page-background pool (8 of 15). See background-01. Also aliased into the note pool as note-05.

background-09.description: Page-background pool (9 of 15) — the old fixed 'recipes' surface-pink value, now just one member of the random pool. See background-01.

background-11.description: Page-background pool (11 of 15) — the old fixed 'home' surface-mint value, now just one member of the random pool. Used as this system's representative default wherever a single page background must be shown. Also aliased into the note pool as note-06.

background-12.description: Page-background pool (12 of 15). See background-01. Also aliased into the note pool as note-07.

background-13.description: Page-background pool (13 of 15) — the old fixed 'blog' surface-cream value, now just one member of the random pool. Also aliased into the note pool as note-08.

background-14.description: Page-background pool (14 of 15). See background-01. Also aliased into the note pool as note-09.

background-15.description: Page-background pool (15 of 15) — the old fixed 'lists' surface-cyan value, now just one member of the random pool. See background-01.

surface-love.description: A warmer alternate note surface (the site's '.draggable.love' variant). Note-pool member only.

surface-note.description: The classic pale-yellow sticky-note surface. Note-pool member only, and this system's representative stand-in for the retired 'highlight' mark.

text-inverse.description: Inverse text on dark or filled surfaces.

text-button-primary.description: Primary (filled) button label. Always white in both themes — no separate hover color has been agreed.

border-default.description: The system's one elevation device: a 1px border on cards, buttons, inputs, and the modal panel, plus the flat hover/focus ring. Replaces the old translucent-ink border everywhere.

border-button-secondary.description: The default button's border — same value as border-default in both themes.

background-button-primary.description: Primary (filled) button background — now the same cyan as accent-primary (the dedicated 'cyan-button' shade was merged into cyan-700). Every primary CTA uses this value in both themes.

accent-primary.description: Interactive emphasis — focus accents and the illustration's primary brand block. Same value as background-button-primary now that they share one cyan.

accent-bright.description: Bright decorative emphasis and active-state surfaces — the illustration's secondary accent block.

space-0.description: Smallest step — hairline gaps/padding, tighter than space-2. (source: 0.25rem)

space-2.description: Half-step — tight gaps (e.g. button icon-to-label gap). (source: 1rem)

space-4.description: The base vertical rhythm unit — card padding, gaps between stacked elements. (source: 2rem)

space-8.description: Double-step — modal/panel padding, generous section spacing. (source: 4rem)

radius-xs.description: Inline code and the smallest marks. (relative unit in source: 0.1em, ~1.6px at a 16px base — actual radius scales with the component's own font-size, not a fixed px value)

radius-sm.description: The default control radius — inputs, plain/icon buttons. Button and Content link chip both moved onto this token at Dani's request ('make the corner radiouses coherent... same feel to it as a button') — Button down from radius-md, the chip up from its own hardcoded 2px — so the two now share one radius instead of each owning a different number. (relative unit in source: 0.3em, ~4.8px at a 16px base — actual radius scales with the component's own font-size, not a fixed px value)

radius-md.description: Cards and the modal panel. Button briefly used this too (see radius-pill below) before moving to radius-sm. (relative unit in source: 0.5em, ~8px at a 16px base — actual radius scales with the component's own font-size, not a fixed px value)

radius-pill.description: Fully pill-shaped elements. No longer used by Button — first moved to radius-md at Dani's request (to read less circular and more like Card's own corner), then to radius-sm (to read coherent with Content link chip) — kept as a token for anything that does want the pill treatment later. (relative unit in source: 2em, ~32px at a 16px base — actual radius scales with the component's own font-size, not a fixed px value)

icon-14.description: Smallest icon size — dense inline contexts (meta text, small labels). Pairs with icon-14-box.

icon-20.description: Default icon size — pairs with icon-20-box. Use this unless a size is called out below.

icon-26.description: Slightly larger — section headers, secondary nav. Pairs with icon-26-box.

icon-40.description: Largest — feature callouts, empty states. Pairs with icon-40-box.

h1.description: Page-level H1 — the per-page headline. Moved here from Display so the full H1–H6 heading ladder lives in one section, but it still renders in the display face (the explicit family override above), not Proza Libre — Display is now reserved for the standalone Page-title treatment only. This cut only ships at regular weight (no bold), so size and the face's own high-contrast serifs carry the emphasis instead of a heavier weight. The display face itself changed at Dani's request, from Heuristica to Infini (a free CC BY-ND typeface by Sandrine Nugue, graphismeenfrance.fr/infini) — Heuristica stays installed and in use only for Rich text's bold-italic emphasis mark, which has no Infini equivalent (no bold-italic cut shipped).

h4.description: Minor headings — same size as body, bold-weight only.

Lead.description: Rich text's lead paragraph -- the display face, one step up from body size. Upright (not italic): it shipped in Heuristica's own italic cut at first, then Dani asked directly for regular instead ("make this lead not italic but regular"). Scoped to .pz-prose-lead only, not applied by any built template on its own. The display face itself moved from Heuristica to Infini at Dani's later request, alongside Page-title/h1 -- same size, weight, line-height and tracking throughout, just a different typeface underneath var(--font-display).

body.description: Paragraphs, list items, default links, card body copy, button labels. Proza Libre's regular cut — this is the system's default font.

small.description: Secondary labels — card role labels, meta text, modal close affordance.

quote.description: The one-sentence pull-quote, set in text-callout color, in Gloria Hallelujah -- the system's deliberate handwritten accent. Previously documented as also covering Return-home navigation's label and Fortune cookie's message -- that was stale: Return-home nav's handwritten styling was removed entirely (see components/HomeNav/README.md), and Fortune cookie's message actually matches the separate Handwritten rung below (16px/20px), not this one. Card's dinner-and-movie-night subtitle (.pz-card-subtitle-callout) is its own 14px size, not claimed to match either rung.

Handwritten.description: The confirmed real use of this style is Fortune cookie's message (.pz-fortune-message), set in Gloria Hallelujah at this size rather than the quote style's larger 19px/25px. Also what Rich text's inline .pz-prose-hand aside uses, per the spec's "supported inline handwritten ... treatments" note, though that class isn't demonstrated in any preview card yet.

button.description: The Button component's label — Proza Libre SemiBold (a real weight, not synthesized), matching Title/body's current size so buttons scale if body type changes. Pill-shaped, bordered, no shadow (see Button in Components); the primary variant fills with background-button-primary and sets this text to text-button-primary (white).

mono.description: New at Dani's request — a fourth family, web-safe monospace (Courier New), bold, 16px with a tight 1:1 16px line-height. For values that benefit from fixed-width characters rather than Proza Libre's proportional spacing — first applied to Business information's copyable fields (tax ID, both addresses, bank account, email).

drop-cap-initial.description: Rich text's drop-cap initial letter (.pz-prose-initial) — always a single uppercase A-Z character, set in Infini Picto's pictogram alphabet. Rendered in a 72px x 72px box with a radius-sm corner and a wavy underline in the live CSS; those are layout/decoration, not part of this text style itself.

card-resting.description: Card at rest — a faint resting shadow, as if sitting flat on a table. Source: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 8%).

card-hover.description: Card on hover — picked up, closer to the light. Source: 0 6px 16px rgb(0 0 0 / 16%).

card-active.description: Card on press/active — held up while being grabbed. Source: 0 8px 20px rgb(0 0 0 / 20%).

note.description: Sticky Note component — an outer drop shadow angled as if lit from one side (pinned to a surface), plus an inner paper-depth shadow and a thin top highlight. Source: 3px 5px 10px rgb(0 0 0 / 20%), inset 0 -10px 14px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 28%), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 35%).

fortune-message.description: Fortune cookie message slip — a slight inset shadow so it reads as a piece of paper, not a lifted card. Source: inset 0 1px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 12%).

midnight.description: Core primitive, dark-mode companion to ink (from pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md). A near-black, cool blue-gray — resolves background-page in dark mode. Does not replace ink; the theme just switches which one background-page points at. Reworked at Dani's request ("the whole dark mode thing has too much and too direct purple in it... can be blue-ish, but not this direct purple") — this used to be #160d1d, a near-black purple; the hue moved toward neutral blue-gray, lightness held the same.

graphite.description: Core primitive, added at Dani's request to pull dark mode's purple back to neutral ("the whole dark mode thing has too much and too direct purple in it... I like all the other darkmode stuff that feels neutral, just the use of purple is too much"). A cool blue-gray slate, lighter than midnight so Card/Lightbox panels still read as a raised surface against the page — resolves surface-near-white in dark mode, replacing the earlier reuse of ink (too purple) there.

surface-near-white.description: The one neutral surface in the system — used by Card, and by the dialog/panel chrome Media lightbox's panel reuses (same value the old 'surface-card' token used). That dialog/panel chrome originally backed a standalone Modal component too; Modal was removed at Dani's request as not needed, but the chrome and this token's use by it stay, since Media lightbox still depends on it. In dark mode this resolves to {graphite} (#252b37), a neutral blue-gray slate — reworked at Dani's request away from its earlier dark value, {ink} (#381652): the dark-mode doc named ink as "the base for tinted surfaces" but didn't address this token directly, and that purple read as too much once seen live, so this is a second pass at the same editorial call, not a reversal of the judgment to need one.

note-01.description: Note/annotation background pool (1 of 9). Same random-per-page-load rule as the page-background pool. Dark value from pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md — the same note reference resolves to a tinted purple instead of a bright pastel; keep the picked reference stable across a theme switch. Reverted to Dani's explicit request ("These sticky notes should remain absolutely the same in dark mode as how they are in light mode!") — the dark value is now a literal copy of the light value rather than a var()-style reference to a primitive that itself changes in dark mode, so Note surfaces (and Link's highlight mark, the pool's other consumer) read identically in both themes.

text-primary.description: Body text and headings. Dark mode uses the warm near-white background-13 pastel as text color (pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md), not a literal white.

text-secondary.description: Secondary text — card role labels, meta text. Same color as text-primary in both themes; dial it back with opacity at the component level (no numeric opacity value has been agreed yet — do not invent one).

text-link.description: Link text (resting and hover — see text-link-hover).

text-link-hover.description: Link text on hover — identical to text-link in light mode. background-link-hover is what changes on hover there, not the text color. In dark mode the hover text itself pales to cyan-100.

text-callout.description: Dedicated color for text set in the callout face (Gloria Hallelujah) — Callout's pull-quote, Return-home navigation's handwritten label, and Fortune cookie's message. Was text-link (light) / text-primary (label only); now its own token so handwritten text no longer borrows a color meant for links or body copy.

background-quote.description: Rich text's quote highlight — a low-alpha tint of text-callout itself, not a separate color, so it stays visually tied to the handwritten face it sits behind. Added at Dani's request, replacing an earlier dotted-separator-above-the-quote treatment he flagged as looking bad ("I have a different idea now. Make it work like having handwritten text, and make it have a slight purple highlight in the background, therefore it looks more like a quote somehow."). Tints blue instead of purple in dark mode since it derives from text-callout's own per-theme value, not a fixed purple. (Briefly replaced with a yellow fill, then restored here at Dani's explicit request to undo that and keep it as it was.)

background-highlight.description: Rich text's in-line yellow highlight mark (.pz-prose-highlight) — split off from surface-note so Note's own frozen-across-themes value isn't disturbed. Light mode is identical to surface-note's pale yellow; dark mode used to be too, until Dani flagged it ("Highlighted text here isn't readable, use a darker or opacity yellow instead of the current one") — against dark mode's near-white text-primary, a near-white yellow highlight is effectively invisible (contrast ~1:1). Dark mode now uses a translucent amber wash over the page instead — same alpha-blend-over-midnight approach as background-quote's own dark value — reading as a darker, more saturated gold than light mode's pastel, with solid (~7.5:1) contrast against the light text sitting on it.

background-initial-invert.description: Rich text's inverted drop-cap variant — a literal, always-opposite fill, at Dani's request ("create an inverted style for it. So put there a body text colored 1:1 block and make the letter white in it. In dark mode invertedly, so white background and bg colored font."). Built from the raw ink/white primitives rather than the semantic text-primary/background-page tokens, since dark mode's text-primary resolves to a warm cream, not true white.

text-initial-invert.description: Letter color for the same inverted drop-cap variant — white on the ink-filled box in light mode, midnight on the white-filled box in dark mode — the same two colors, just which one is background and which is text flips.

text-note.description: Text set on a note/annotation background (the note-pool). Added for pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md; reserved for a future dedicated note/annotation card — today the note pool is only consumed as the Link highlight mark, which sits under ambient text-primary. Reverted alongside note-01..09 — Dani asked that sticky notes look absolutely the same in dark mode as in light mode, so this now stays {ink} in both themes instead of paling to background-13.

border-strong.description: A stronger border where more contrast than border-default is needed. The dark-mode doc warned that reusing ink here would be nearly invisible on midnight but didn't specify a replacement, so this is an editorial call — background-13 for maximum contrast; flag if you'd rather something else.

border-button-primary.description: The primary button's 1px outline, added for pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md (previously the border just reused background-button-primary inline in bundle.css). Same cyan-700 value in both themes.

background-link-hover.description: Hover-state background behind a link. Dark value is the resolved 14% cyan-500 + 86% midnight sRGB blend from pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md (token aliases can't carry color-mix(), so this is the pre-computed hex) — recomputed after midnight itself moved from purple to blue-gray at Dani's request, so this stays the correct blend of the two.

background-page.description: Theme-aware page background. Light mode's true behavior is still the random background-01..15 pool (background-11 here is just this system's representative stand-in, per background-11's own note); dark mode is fixed to the midnight primitive — pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md keeps the dark page flat rather than randomized.

surface-interactive.description: Default (resting) background for Button, Clickable icon, Clickable icon+text and Clickable chip — a faint tinted wash (ink at light mode, background-13 at dark mode, both under 8% alpha) rather than fully transparent, so these controls read as clickable at rest, per Dani's October 2026 'atomic clickables' restyle. Pre-computed alpha hex, same pattern as --transparent and background-link-hover's dark blend — token aliases can't carry alpha onto a referenced value.

surface-interactive-hover.description: Hover background for the same clickable family, paired with a border-default border — Dani's own 'white bg... on hover' call for light mode, where a literal white hover on a near-white page is the right amount of lift. The earlier dark-mode value (a flagged editorial call, resolving to the solid background-13 near-white at full opacity) was exactly what Dani then flagged: 'this should not be filled with white on hover... rich lighter background, like 2% of white fill, so not fully white.' Dark now uses the same background-13 color as a translucent wash instead — pre-computed alpha hex (token aliases can't carry alpha onto a referenced value), sitting between surface-interactive's ~8% resting wash and surface-interactive-active's ~16% wash rather than jumping to an opaque fill.

surface-interactive-active.description: Pressed/active background for the same clickable family — a stronger version of surface-interactive's own wash, for 'a darker bg than original on click.' Pre-computed alpha hex, same pattern as surface-interactive.

glow-interactive.description: The hover/focus glow for the whole clickable family — cyan-500 (accent-bright) at ~40% alpha, used as a tight, low-blur box-shadow rather than a soft decorative one ('a slight bluish glow (not too blurred)'). Replaces the old plain grey box-shadow ring Button's hover used to show. Same value in both themes since it's already a bright, saturated accent that reads clearly on either background-page.

midnight.description: Core primitive, dark-mode companion to ink (from pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md). A near-black, cool blue-gray — resolves background-page in dark mode. Does not replace ink; the theme just switches which one background-page points at. Reworked at Dani's request ("the whole dark mode thing has too much and too direct purple in it... can be blue-ish, but not this direct purple") — this used to be #160d1d, a near-black purple; the hue moved toward neutral blue-gray, lightness held the same.

background-initial-invert.description: Rich text's inverted drop-cap variant — a literal, always-opposite fill, at Dani's request ("create an inverted style for it. So put there a body text colored 1:1 block and make the letter white in it. In dark mode invertedly, so white background and bg colored font."). Built from the raw ink/white primitives rather than the semantic text-primary/background-page tokens, since dark mode's text-primary resolves to a warm cream, not true white.

text-initial-invert.description: Letter color for the same inverted drop-cap variant — white on the ink-filled box in light mode, midnight on the white-filled box in dark mode — the same two colors, just which one is background and which is text flips.

text-note.description: Text set on a note/annotation background (the note-pool). Added for pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md; reserved for a future dedicated note/annotation card — today the note pool is only consumed as the Link highlight mark, which sits under ambient text-primary. Reverted alongside note-01..09 — Dani asked that sticky notes look absolutely the same in dark mode as in light mode, so this now stays {ink} in both themes instead of paling to background-13.

border-strong.description: A stronger border where more contrast than border-default is needed. The dark-mode doc warned that reusing ink here would be nearly invisible on midnight but didn't specify a replacement, so this is an editorial call — background-13 for maximum contrast; flag if you'd rather something else.

border-button-primary.description: The primary button's 1px outline, added for pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md (previously the border just reused background-button-primary inline in bundle.css). Same cyan-700 value in both themes.

background-link-hover.description: Hover-state background behind a link. Dark value is the resolved 14% cyan-500 + 86% midnight sRGB blend from pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md (token aliases can't carry color-mix(), so this is the pre-computed hex) — recomputed after midnight itself moved from purple to blue-gray at Dani's request, so this stays the correct blend of the two.

background-page.description: Theme-aware page background. Light mode's true behavior is still the random background-01..15 pool (background-11 here is just this system's representative stand-in, per background-11's own note); dark mode is fixed to the midnight primitive — pucz-hu-dark-mode-design-system.md keeps the dark page flat rather than randomized.

surface-interactive.description: Default (resting) background for Button, Clickable icon, Clickable icon+text and Clickable chip — a faint tinted wash (ink at light mode, background-13 at dark mode, both under 8% alpha) rather than fully transparent, so these controls read as clickable at rest, per Dani's October 2026 'atomic clickables' restyle. Pre-computed alpha hex, same pattern as --transparent and background-link-hover's dark blend — token aliases can't carry alpha onto a referenced value.

surface-interactive-hover.description: Hover background for the same clickable family, paired with a border-default border — Dani's own 'white bg... on hover' call for light mode, where a literal white hover on a near-white page is the right amount of lift. The earlier dark-mode value (a flagged editorial call, resolving to the solid background-13 near-white at full opacity) was exactly what Dani then flagged: 'this should not be filled with white on hover... rich lighter background, like 2% of white fill, so not fully white.' Dark now uses the same background-13 color as a translucent wash instead — pre-computed alpha hex (token aliases can't carry alpha onto a referenced value), sitting between surface-interactive's ~8% resting wash and surface-interactive-active's ~16% wash rather than jumping to an opaque fill.

surface-interactive-active.description: Pressed/active background for the same clickable family — a stronger version of surface-interactive's own wash, for 'a darker bg than original on click.' Pre-computed alpha hex, same pattern as surface-interactive.

glow-interactive.description: The hover/focus glow for the whole clickable family — cyan-500 (accent-bright) at ~40% alpha, used as a tight, low-blur box-shadow rather than a soft decorative one ('a slight bluish glow (not too blurred)'). Replaces the old plain grey box-shadow ring Button's hover used to show. Same value in both themes since it's already a bright, saturated accent that reads clearly on either background-page.
